questions.question: 1. What is true about the time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm?

answers.a: Best case is when given graph is a tree itself
answers.b: Worst case is when all edges are to be checked.
answers.c: Time complexity is O(E log(V) + E log(E)), where E is the number of edges and V is the number of Vertices

explanations.a: Incorrect. Best case is when given graph is a tree itself is correct, but there are more options which can be true.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Worst case is when all edges are to be checked is correct, but there are more options which can be true.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Time complexity is correct, but there are more options which can be true.
explanations.d: Correct. All of the given statements about Kruskal's algorithm time complexity are true.

questions.question: 2. Can Kruskal's algorithm produce more than one MST without any changes in the code?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Kruskal's algorithm can produce different MSTs only if equal weighted edges are handled differently.
explanations.b: Correct. Kruskal’s cannot produce any different MST, if the edge selection is not modified or randomised, for equal weighing edges.
explanations.c: Incorrect. It depends on how equal weighted edges are handled.
explanations.d: Incorrect. We can determine whether different MSTs can be produced.

questions.question: 3. What is the best case Time Complexity of Kruskal's Algorithm? (Let V be the number of vertices, E be the number of edges)

explanations.a: Correct. In the best case, Kruskal's algorithm needs to check only V-1 edges to build the MST, resulting in O((V-1)log(E)+Elog(E)) time complexity.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This doesn't represent the best case time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This doesn't represent the best case time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Option a represents the correct best case time complexity.

questions.question: 4. In which scenario, Kruskal’s algorithm will result in the best time complexity?

answers.a: Maximum number of edges and maximum number of cycles
answers.b: Maximum number of edges and minimum number of cycles
answers.c: Minimum number of edges and maximum number of cycles
answers.d: Minimum number of edges and minimum number of cycles

explanations.a: Incorrect. Maximum number of edges and cycles would result in worst case performance.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Maximum number of edges would still require many iterations.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Maximum number of cycles requires many cycle detection operations.
explanations.d: Correct. Kruskal's Algorithm picks one edge every time to build a MST, and uses a disjoint set data structure to check for cycles. Hence it will perform fastest when there will be the least number of edges and cycles present in the graph.
